newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn futures close firm before USDA reports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn futures close firm before USDA reports.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed firmer on short covering before the release at 0730 CST Tuesday of USDA's November crop production and supply/demand reports, traders said.
"It's short covering, evening up of positions before tomorrow's report," said Paul Haugens, vice president of FIMAT Futures. "The market was short plus people are looking for a post-harvest rally."
Friday's Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders Report showed as of November 5, funds were short corn by a roughly three to one ratio.
Slow farmer selling and harvest slowdowns in the eastern U.S. growing region were mentioned as supportive factors.

Traders remained skeptical of reports of another possible trade conflict with China. China said it expected talks with the United States soon on a dispute over U.S. sanctions on its textiles and its own threat to retaliate.
Volume was light with E.D. and F. Man International a buyer of two million bushels of December and Farmers Commodities Corp bought 1.5 million December, they said.
Corn closed 3/4 cent per bushel higher to 1/2 lower, with December up 3/4 at $2.68-1/4.

Traders said the market was short term oversold but December's nine day relative strength index (RSI) was moving into neutral territory and closed at 42.5 points, nearly midway between oversold at 30 and overbought at 70.
Longer term indicators remained bearish with the key moving averages continuing to point downward, technicians reported.

First resistance in the December was at $2.69-1/4 and second resistance was at $2.73-3/4. The session high for December was $2.69-3/4. First support was at $2.64-3/4 and second support was at $2.60-1/4.
Corn futures volume was at 80,000 contracts, below the 82,340 traded Friday, according to the CBOT.

In corn options, Cargill Investor Services bought 1,000 December $2.50 puts at 1/2 cent, Term Commodities bought 400 December $2.60 puts at 1-7/8, bought 400 March $2.60 puts and sold 400 March $2.90 calls at one cent, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 23,000 contracts, below the 35,775 traded Friday.
